risks.message: 4 SQL statements executed on every iteration of this LOOP (lines 38, 60, 62, 65): one database round-trip each per row. Prefer set-based statements.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Collapse per-row statements inside loops into one set-based statement.

architectural_decisions.decision: Collapsed the per-row loop (fee lookup, debit, TARIFA insert, audit insert) into set-based statements sharing one CTE; the debit aggregates fees per account before UPDATE ... FROM.
architectural_decisions.rationale: UPDATE ... FROM applies at most one source row per target, so per-account aggregation is required when one account has several fees; set-based execution removes 4 round-trips per row.

architectural_decisions.decision: No commit/rollback in the function; all statements run on the caller's connection/transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The original procedure had no transaction control of its own.

architectural_decisions.decision: All SQL statements are module-level literal constants passed to sqlalchemy.text(); no string building at call sites.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Avoids S608 and any injection surface; bind parameters are the only variable parts.

warnings: The CASE over v_tipo was corrected: TRANSFERENCIA keeps the fee unchanged (v_taxa := v_taxa), SAQUE multiplies by 1.10, any other tipo by 0.90. The previous version wrongly applied 1.10 to TRANSFERENCIA.

v_taxa is declared plain NUMERIC (unbounded) in the original, so no intermediate rounding is applied in the CTE; rounding happens only when values are written to the NUMERIC(18,2) columns (transacoes.valor, contas.saldo), matching PL/pgSQL behaviour.
v_total_taxas is treated as initialized to 0 (validation showed the original logs total_taxas 0 for an empty batch), implemented as COALESCE(SUM(taxa), 0).
The summary log row is written even when the reference date is NULL or no transactions match, with transacoes 0 and total_taxas 0, as in the original.
Ties in taxas.vigente_de are resolved by an arbitrary LIMIT 1, exactly as the original ORDER BY vigente_de DESC LIMIT 1.
